declared.title: Experienced well-being rises with income, even above $75,000 per year
declared.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « experienced well-being rises with income beyond 75000 » (2026-11-22)

population: employed US adults, 1,725,994 momentary reports collected by a smartphone app (Track Your Happiness)

findings.text: Both feelings in the moment and satisfaction with life rise with each doubling of income, as steeply for high earners as for low earners

support.sentence: Drawing on 1,725,994 experience-sampling reports from 33,391 employed US adults, the present results show that both experienced and evaluative well-being increased linearly with log(income), with an equally steep slope for higher earners as for lower earners.

findings.text: No plateau of day-to-day well-being above $75,000 a year

support.sentence: There was no evidence for an experienced well-being plateau above $75,000/y, contrary to some influential past research.

limits: an association: income is not manipulated
self-selected users of a happiness-tracking app, employed US adults only: not representative
the 2023 reanalysis with Kahneman finds a plateau after all in the least happy fifth of this same sample
